title: When the West Gets Weird
body:
https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=CYvruxt8Ocw

Daniel (@dungeondive) uses his love of Shadows of Brimstone as the springboard for a deep dive into western and weird-western fiction — a genre he adores and defends against its many detractors. He starts with the straight stuff: Larry McMurtry's *Lonesome Dove* (his favourite novel, "Lord of the Rings set in the American West"), Elmore Leonard's western stories, and *The Ox-Bow Incident*. Then the weird West proper: Robert E. Howard as a godfather, Joe R. Lansdale's *Dead Man's Road* collection as the perfect entry point, and Charles G. Finney's astonishing *The Circus of Dr. Lao*. He saves his top tier for two series — Edward M. Erdelac's *Merkabah Rider*, a Jewish-mystic gunslinger fusing Lovecraft with Kabbalah, and Stephen King's *Dark Tower*, which he's read seven times and calls the best reading experience of his life. He rounds out with R.S. Belcher's *Six-Gun Tarot*, Catherynne M. Valente's *Six-Gun Snow White*, and an *Encyclopedia of Weird Westerns* to map further reading. Essential viewing for anyone whose Brimstone campaign left them hungry for the fiction behind the theme.

----

The weird West is a small, strange shelf. What's the strongest one you'd press into Daniel's hands — a book, a comic, or even a film?
